doc.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Mark Murphy
summary: Mark Murphy was among the thirteen singers for Sing a Song of Basie and became a lifelong committed jazz singer.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Mark Murphy was one of the 13 singers we hired to do Sing a Song of Basie. His eyes were always like this at what we were doing. He wasn’t particularly a jazz singer then. He had been an accountant, I think. He was amazed at the whole thing. He would come down to the house every day. Even when we had no rehearsals, he would be there. From what we were doing, and from just listening to Dave and I talk, and then me talking to him, he became a jazz singer, and he’s never turned his back. I’ve got the greatest respect for him, because this man never turned away from jazz singing. He always – his is right now – wherever you find Mark Murphy, you find a jazz singer. I admire him for that. I admire him highly for that.
I make it a point to always see him as well.
He’s true to the art form.
“This could be the start of something big.” You really turned that around.
